resources.string: People who haven\'t messaged you yet
Give a voice and a ringtone to someone before they message you.
The WhatsApp entries your phone\'s contacts already hold: each person\'s name and WhatsApp number. WhatsApp itself puts them there.
Your messages, chats and groups, or any of WhatsApp\'s files. Nothing else about your contacts either.
Only the people you pick. Nothing leaves your phone.
Why it asks for your contacts
Android keeps these entries with your contacts, so Cucuto needs permission to read them. It is the same permission phone ringtones use.

WhatsApp names a chat only when it messages you. So when someone you add first writes, Cucuto checks their name against these entries and links the chat. That first message plays WhatsApp\'s tone; their voice plays from the next one. Phone ringtones work right away.
Pick who you want to give a voice. Only they are saved.
Your contacts have no WhatsApp entries. WhatsApp adds them when it is allowed to see your contacts. People who message you still show up on Home.
Without the contacts permission, Cucuto can\'t see the WhatsApp entries. People who message you still show up on Home. You can allow it in Android\'s settings at any time.
Android won\'t ask again. Allow it in Android\'s settings, under Permissions, then Contacts. When you come back, the list opens.
Their first message plays WhatsApp\'s tone and links the chat. Their voice plays from the next one; phone ringtones work right away.
Not linked yet: waits for their first message
Someone you added has this name. Tap to say who it is.
Pick a character. %1$s\'s voice plays once their first message links the chat.
A chat named %1$s messaged you. More than one person could be %1$s, so Cucuto won\'t guess. Check the number in WhatsApp, then pick who it is. Their voice plays from their next message.
Cucuto links this chat when %1$s first messages you on WhatsApp. That first message plays WhatsApp\'s tone; the voice plays from the next one. A phone ringtone works right away.
